data.why: The app's Structural validation and CYP Blind Challenge tabs read checked-in repo files (data/boltz_test/validation_summary.json, data/cyp_challenge/structure_track_test_blinded.csv); the Motif screen tab needs a SMILES file to paste/upload, so a sample file with the four reference compounds, one motif-negative compound (aspirin), and one deliberately invalid SMILES was written for the browser to use.

goals: Screen a list of candidate compounds for classic heme-coordinating (Type II) CYP450 inhibition motifs by pasting or uploading SMILES
Download the motif-screen results as a CSV for further analysis

Inspect which of four cryo-EM-solved reference compounds (ketoconazole, ritonavir, azamulin, vardenafil) are structurally confirmed to coordinate the heme iron versus which are motif-positive but not coordinated
Compare the motif screen's calls against the OpenADMET CYP Blind Challenge's blinded structure-prediction test set and see which compounds already have completed structural validation

review.summary: The tree accurately covers all three tabs of this small Streamlit app in a sensible order (screen, then confirm against structure, then apply to the blinded benchmark), and all ten screens I opened show what their nodes claim. Before filing it needs a few fixes: the goal overstates the structural check, which covers only four precomputed reference compounds; the CSV-upload pitfall is missing; t10 duplicates t2/t4; and grid-toolbar steps are presented as app features.
